title: bug: VS Code runs vm-control with the full extension-host env, while JetBrains scrubs it under the protected profile
description:
Found in the CQ-I06f whole-epic review at 96f7bdd4 (I05 residual). JetBrains ManagedVmPanel.execute applies supervisor.protectedDaemonEnvironment(builder.environment()) when RuntimeSelectionPolicy.profile is PROTECTED (ManagedVmPanel.kt:117-122). VS Code ManagedVmTreeProvider.execute (:75-80) calls runVmControl(execFile, ...), whose options (ManagedVm.ts:96) carry no env. The child therefore inherits every extension-host variable, including MOE_RUNNER_STATE_DIR, which picks the VM ledger dir (vm-control.mjs ownedLedgerDir).
This is latent while verified-local is unavailable (the daemon refuses with EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY). It must be at parity before strong-profile activation.
definitionOfDone: Under a protected (verified-local) read, VS Code runs vm-control with the same scrubbed environment JetBrains uses; legacy/observe stays unchanged.
A moe-vscode node:test pins the env passed to execFile for both profiles.
cd moe-vscode && npm test passes in a snapshot.

implementationPlan.note: Created moe-vscode/tests/managed-vm-runtime.test.cjs (10 node:test cases: R1 x2 profiles, R2 x3, R3 x2, R4 x3). RED run in place under WSL node 24.21 (node --test only, no npm): 3 pass, 7 fail. R2 (legacy/observe/absent) passes against HEAD, which is the characterization of today's call. R1 (no env, legacy-node used), R3 (no node-missing; legacy path ran) and R4 (protectedVmControlRuntime is not a function) fail for the intended reasons. Loader: same-realm vm.runInThisContext wrapper with injected process, fresh module instances per fixture so the session pin cannot leak. Dirty paths owned by other sessions (.moe task JSONs, getCommitScope.*, postflight-worktree.cjs, .moe/decisions) left untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN: three edits, with JetBrains ManagedVmPanel.execute and nodeCommand (moe-jetbrains/.../toolwindow/ManagedVmPanel.kt) as the reference.

(a) src/util/ManagedVm.ts. Task-01020adf's CODE_TEXT edits may already be in the file; leave them and everything else alone.
- Add `env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv` to ExecFileLike's options type, and a trailing optional `env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv` parameter to runVmControl.
- Spread env into options only when it is given, `...(env ? { env } : {})`, so a legacy call builds exactly today's options object: no env key, not even env: undefined.
- Doc comment: without env the child inherits the extension host's environment (legacy, observe); a protected run passes protectedVmControlRuntime's env.
- The module stays require-free, because managed-vm.test.cjs throws on any require.

(b) src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts: after protectedDaemonEnvironment, and WITHOUT changing it, add `export function protectedVmControlRuntime(basePath: string, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env, windows = process.platform === 'win32', home = env.HOME || env.USERPROFILE): { node: string; env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv } | undefined`.
- node = installedExecutable(protectedNodeCandidate(env, home, windows, basePath), basePath). On 'rejected', return undefined; selectInstalledFile already logs the reason, and no UI text is added.
- The env is a copy of env:
  - every NODE_OPTIONS or NODE_PATH key is removed, case-insensitively on Windows and exactly elsewhere (the predicate protectedDaemonEnvironment uses);
  - on Windows, only the first of pathNames(copy, windows) is kept and the other PATH-like keys are deleted;
  - when that key holds a value, it becomes protectedPathEntries(value, basePath).join(path.delimiter).
- Nothing is added (no dirname(node), no ~/.local/share/moe dirs) and nothing is deduplicated. An absent PATH stays absent. Every other variable is kept, MOE_RUNNER_STATE_DIR included: vm-control.mjs ownedLedgerDir uses it to find the runner's ledger, and JetBrains keeps it.
- Doc comment: this is the VS Code mirror of ManagedVmPanel's protected run, nodeCommand plus MoeDaemonSupervisor.protectedDaemonEnvironment without applyDaemonPath. It is stricter only where VS Code already is (Windows case variants, duplicate PATH keys).

(c) src/providers/ManagedVmTreeProvider.ts execute:
- Keep the no-project and script-missing checks first.
- Then `if (runtimeProfile(root) !== 'protected') { return runVmControl(execFile, this.client.resolveDaemonRuntime().node, script, command, root, signal); }`, which is today's call byte for byte.
- Otherwise `const runtime = protectedVmControlRuntime(root); return runtime ? runVmControl(execFile, runtime.node, script, command, root, signal, runtime.env) : Promise.resolve(unreadable('node-missing'));`.
- Import runtimeProfile and protectedVmControlRuntime from '../services/MoeDaemonClient'. Today only the MoeDaemonClient type is imported.
- Add one comment line naming the JetBrains counterpart.

ERROR HANDLING: add no new throw or reject path.
- A refused protected node is the fixed unreadable('node-missing'): no process, no legacy fallback, no path in UI text.
- runtimeProfile never throws; it fails closed to protected.
- protectedVmControlRuntime catches nothing new, because installedExecutable and protectedPathEntries never throw.
- runVmControl keeps its try/catch and callback mapping, so execute still always resolves.
- run()'s `.catch(() => unreadable('failed'))` stays.

Re-run the step-1 file: GREEN.
implementationPlan.note: GREEN. ManagedVm.ts: ExecFileLike options gain env?, runVmControl a trailing optional env spread only when given (legacy builds no env key); still require-free. MoeDaemonClient.ts: new export protectedVmControlRuntime(basePath, env, windows, home) = installedExecutable(protectedNodeCandidate) + copy of env minus NODE_OPTIONS/NODE_PATH, first PATH key filtered by protectedPathEntries, duplicates dropped; no applyDaemonPath, no dedupe; protectedDaemonEnvironment untouched. ManagedVmTreeProvider.execute: non-protected keeps today's call byte for byte; protected uses the helper, refused node gives unreadable('node-missing') with no process and no legacy fallback. managed-vm-runtime.test.cjs run in place under WSL node 24.21 (node --test only): 10/10 pass (R1 x2, R2 x3, R3 x2, R4 x3). Dirty paths owned by other sessions (.moe task JSONs, .moe/decisions) untouched.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Under a protected read (runtimeProfile(root) === 'protected', meaning verified-local, a session pin or a fail-closed project.json), the VS Code Managed VMs view runs vm-control.mjs as JetBrains ManagedVmPanel.execute does. The executable is the protected node selection: protectedNodeCandidate validated by installedExecutable. When that selection is refused, the view returns unreadable 'node-missing' and starts no process. The environment is a copy of the extension-host env without NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH, whose PATH keeps only protectedPathEntries; nothing is added and every other variable, MOE_RUNNER_STATE_DIR included, is kept. Legacy, observe and an absent profile keep today's call exactly: resolveDaemonRuntime().node, with execFile options that have no env key, so the child inherits the extension-host env.
acceptanceCriteria: Protected read: execFile receives the installedExecutable-accepted real node path, and options.env equals the extension-host env minus NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH, with PATH filtered by protectedPathEntries, nothing added and all other variables kept.
Protected read with a refused node: resolves {kind:'unreadable', reason:'node-missing'}, starts no process and never consults resolveDaemonRuntime.
Legacy, observe and an absent project.json: execFile receives resolveDaemonRuntime().node and options {timeout, maxBuffer, windowsHide, signal?} with no own env key, as at HEAD.
The extension-host env object is never mutated, and execute never rejects.
moe-vscode/tests/managed-vm-runtime.test.cjs pins all of the above with exact values (R1-R3 through ManagedVmTreeProvider.execute; R4 covers the helper's Windows and POSIX branches).
The step-3 snapshot gate (npm ci, lint, compile, test) exits 0.
invariants: A protected read never runs vm-control with the legacy node or with the unscrubbed environment.
Every variable JetBrains keeps for vm-control is kept, MOE_RUNNER_STATE_DIR in particular.
The caller's env object is never mutated, and the view's run still always resolves to a report.
compatibility: Legacy and observe vm-control runs are unchanged: the same node source and the same options object, with no env key.
protectedDaemonEnvironment, startProtectedDaemon and resolveDaemonRuntime are unchanged; protected-daemon-spawn.test.cjs passes untouched.
ManagedVm.ts stays require-free. CODE_TEXT, decode and the rendered texts (including task-01020adf's additions) are untouched, and no new UI text is added.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Reuse VS Code protectedDaemonEnvironment as-is: REJECTED. It is JetBrains applyDaemonPath plus the scrub, so PATH gains dirname(node), the ~/.local/share/moe bootstrap dirs and a dedupe. JetBrains ManagedVmPanel applies the scrub alone, so that would not be the same environment JetBrains uses (DoD 1).
2. Scrub the env but keep resolveDaemonRuntime().node under protected: REJECTED. An unvalidated MOE_NODE_COMMAND, or a bare 'node', would defeat the scrub and diverge from JetBrains nodeCommand, which validates with installedExecutable and returns NODE_MISSING.
3. Also scrub MOE_RUNNER_STATE_DIR (the description names it): REJECTED. JetBrains keeps it, and vm-control.mjs ownedLedgerDir must read the same ledger the runner writes.
4. Refactor protectedDaemonEnvironment to share the new scrub: REJECTED. It touches the certified daemon-spawn path (tests D1, D6, D7) for no behaviour gain.
5. Test only the helper plus runVmControl: REJECTED as the only test. The defect sits in the provider's wiring, so R1-R3 drive ManagedVmTreeProvider.execute through a recording execFile, and R4 covers the Windows branch on any host.

completionSummary:
Under a protected profile (verified-local, session pin or fail-closed project.json), the VS Code Managed VMs view now runs vm-control.mjs like JetBrains ManagedVmPanel.execute does. The executable is the installed-executable-validated protected node. The env is a copy of the extension-host env without NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH, with PATH filtered by protectedPathEntries. Nothing is added or deduplicated, and MOE_RUNNER_STATE_DIR and every other variable are kept. A refused node resolves unreadable 'node-missing' with no process and no legacy fallback. Legacy, observe and absent project.json keep HEAD's call byte for byte: resolveDaemonRuntime().node with options that have no env key.
